message:
I see the `pj_init_plus_ctx` function. The `MAX_ARG` is 200, and there's a check `if( argc+1 == MAX_ARG )` before adding to argv. But wait - this check is `argc+1 == MAX_ARG`, which means when argc is 199, argc+1 is 200, so it errors. But what if argc is already 200? Let me trace through this more carefully.

Actually, looking at the loop: when `argc+1 == MAX_ARG` (i.e., argc == 199), it errors. So the maximum argc is 199, and argv[198] is the last valid index. This seems safe.

Let me look at the `get_init` function which handles `+init` parameters - this is where file-based initialization happens and could have array issues:

<｜｜DSML｜｜
<parameter=command>sed -n '120,280p' /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/proj.4/src/pj_init.c</｜｜DSML｜｜>
</｜｜DSML｜｜>
